Demographic data within the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] provides a comprehensive overview of the populations undergoing ADHD assessment and treatment in Denmark. This data is critical for understanding patient flows, gender distributions, and regional variations in healthcare delivery. The database primarily divides its demographic tracking into two main groups: the [[adhd-udredningspopulation|ADHD-udredningspopulation]] (assessment population) and the [[adhd-behandlingspopulation|ADHD-behandlingspopulation]] (treatment population).

Between April 1, 2023, and March 31, 2024, the assessment population comprised 5,215 assessment courses, while the treatment population included 3,414 patients in package courses [^src1]. Gender demographics show a clear majority of boys in both groups, accounting for 59% of the assessment population and 62% of the treatment population [^src1]. Regional breakdowns also highlight specific demographic gaps; for example, in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], there were no registered patients in the 0–5 age group within the treatment population during this period [^src1].

Beyond pediatric and adolescent data, the demographic scope also covers adult patients. The majority of adult Danes with ADHD are assessed and treated in private specialist practices [^src2]. To monitor the quality and demographic focus of adult care, specific indicators are utilized. [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] specifically relates to adults (18+ years) and was notably reported for the first time without historical data or trend graphs [^src3]. Similarly, [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] is another metric dedicated to tracking the adult demographic (18+ years) [^src4].
